mainTopic: The cabbage ספיחין dispute between רבי שמעון and חכמים, a traveler's customs about working on ערב פסח, and the start of a discussion on יום טוב שני
overview: This amud finishes a story that began on the previous דף. A teacher ate cabbage ספיחין during שביעית and let his student eat them, but only in the teacher's presence. The teacher had personally seen רבי שמעון בן יוחי eat them, and the student had not. The גמרא quotes a ברייתא in which רבי שמעון permits cabbage ספיחין and the חכמים forbid all ספיחין. It shows that both sides accept רבי עקיבא's source for the איסור of ספיחין. Their only disagreement is whether to make a גזירה on cabbage because of other ספיחין. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about a traveler between towns with different customs about working on ערב פסח, and asks how 'a person should not deviate because of dispute' fits the case of someone arriving in a town that works. אביי answers that the phrase applies only to the first case. רבא answers that refraining from work is no deviation, because onlookers will assume he is simply idle. Finally, רב ספרא begins a question to רבי אבא about יום טוב שני for communities that know the calendar, and the question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The teacher eats cabbage after-growths and lets his student eat only in his presence
steps.stepSummary: The story continues. The teacher eats cabbage ספיחין and gives some to his student. He tells him to eat only while the teacher is present.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he took cabbage after-growths, ate, and gave some to me. He said to me: My son, in my presence you may eat; not in my presence, do not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story from the previous דף. A teacher ate cabbage that grew by itself in שביעית and let his student eat it too, but only while the teacher was there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story serves as a precedent about relying on a חכם's practice. The teacher permits the food, but the student's permission depends on the teacher being present. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: Cabbage after-growths: cabbage that grew by itself during שביעית without being planted

phrases.english: And he took cabbage after-growths
phrases.notes: These grew by themselves during the שביעית year.

phrases.english: and ate, and gave to me,
and he said to me: My son,
in my presence, eat;
not in my presence, do not eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנָטַל סְפִיחֵי כְרוּב וְאָכַל וְנָתַן לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a story begun on the previous דף.
steps.raayaObject: Whether one may rely on having seen a חכם act leniently.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teacher's own practice of eating cabbage ספיחין and his instruction to his student.

steps.title: Why the student may eat only in the teacher's presence
steps.stepSummary: The teacher saw רבי שמעון בן יוחי eat cabbage ספיחין himself, so he may always rely on that. The student knows only through the teacher, so he may rely on it only in the teacher's presence.
steps.simpleTranslation: I, who saw רבי שמעון בן יוחי eat, can say that רבי שמעון בן יוחי is worthy to rely on, both in his presence and not in his presence. You may eat in my presence; not in my presence, do not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The teacher explains his rule. He personally saw רבי שמעון בן יוחי eat cabbage ספיחין, but the student did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An eyewitness to a גדול's practice may rely on it fully, even when that גדול is not around. Someone who knows only secondhand may rely on it only while the eyewitness teacher is present to stand behind it. The point is about how far a lenient practice may be passed down, not about whether cabbage is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: That I saw (I was an eyewitness)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two 'presences.' The teacher could rely on רבי שמעון בן יוחי even when רבי שמעון was absent. The student may rely on the teacher only while the teacher is there.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a lenient practice someone saw firsthand carries more weight than one only heard about.

phrases.english: I, who saw

phrases.aramaic: אֶת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי שֶׁאָכַל —
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai eat,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדַי הוּא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai is worthy
to rely upon him
both in his presence and not in his presence.
You, in my presence, eat;
phrases.notes: The student did not see רבי שמעון בן יוחי himself.

phrases.english: not in my presence, do not eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנִי שֶׁרָאִיתִי אֶת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי שֶׁאָכַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for the instruction in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An eyewitness may rely on a גדול's practice everywhere. One who heard only secondhand may rely on it only in the eyewitness's presence.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון's ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly רבי שמעון's ruling on cabbage ספיחין is, so it can see it recorded in a source.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the ruling of רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns from the story to the הלכה behind it. This short question sets up the next step, which quotes the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story assumed that רבי שמעון בן יוחי permitted cabbage ספיחין. The גמרא wants to see that ruling written in a source.

phrases.english: What is the view of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling the story relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The text of רבי שמעון's position on ספיחין.

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי שמעון permits cabbage after-growths, the חכמים forbid all
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records the dispute. רבי שמעון forbids all ספיחין except cabbage, because cabbage is unlike field vegetables. The חכמים forbid all ספיחין.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי שמעון says all after-growths are forbidden, except cabbage after-growths, since nothing like them is found among field vegetables. And the חכמים say all after-growths are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a ברייתא that shows the מחלוקת between רבי שמעון and the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that ספיחין are generally forbidden. רבי שמעון makes an exception for cabbage because it does not resemble ordinary field vegetables. The חכמים make no exception.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
After-growths: produce that sprouted by itself in שביעית

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
All after-growths are forbidden,
except for cabbage after-growths,
since there is nothing like them among the field vegetables.
And the Sages say:
All after-growths are forbidden.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא: רבי שמעון exempts cabbage ספיחין from the איסור, while the חכמים forbid all ספיחין.

steps.title: Both sides follow רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that both רבי שמעון and the חכמים hold like רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both of them hold in accordance with רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a claim that both opinions start from the same base. This line sets up the next step, which brings רבי עקיבא's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying both follow רבי עקיבא, the גמרא shows they agree on the basic איסור of ספיחין. Their dispute must therefore be about something narrower.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with the view of

phrases.english: And both of them hold in accordance with Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places the dispute of step 4 within רבי עקיבא's framework.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both רבי שמעון and the חכמים accept רבי עקיבא's view that ספיחין are forbidden.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns the איסור of ספיחין from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא asks why the פסוק mentions gathering if no one sows in שביעית. He concludes that the gathering refers to ספיחין, which are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'Behold, we may not sow nor gather our crops.' רבי עקיבא said: Since they do not sow, from where would they gather? From here we learn that after-growths are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא with רבי עקיבא's source for the איסור of ספיחין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If nothing is planted in שביעית, there seems to be nothing to gather. So the פסוק's 'not gather' must mean things that grew by themselves. That is how רבי עקיבא learns that ספיחין are forbidden.

phrases.english: As it was taught: 'Behold, we may not sow,'
'nor gather our crops,'
Rabbi Akiva said:
And since they do not sow,
from where would they gather?
From here we learn that after-growths are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: ״הֵן לֹא נִזְרָע וְלֹא נֶאֱסֹף אֶת תְּבוּאָתֵנוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That ספיחין are forbidden according to רבי עקיבא, as the base both sides share.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's דרשה on the פסוק 'הן לא נזרע ולא נאסף'.

steps.title: What is the actual point of disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: Both sides agree with רבי עקיבא, so the גמרא asks what they argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: With regard to what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the dispute is really about. This question sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once both sides accept that ספיחין are forbidden, the reason for רבי שמעון's exception for cabbage needs to be explained.

phrases.english: With regard to what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 6: since both share the source, it asks what the dispute is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that divides רבי שמעון and the חכמים.

steps.title: The dispute is whether to make a decree on cabbage because of other after-growths
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים make a גזירה on cabbage ספיחין because of other ספיחין. רבי שמעון does not make that גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים hold: We make a decree on cabbage after-growths because of other after-growths in general. And רבי שמעון holds: We do not make a decree on cabbage after-growths because of other after-growths in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the whole dispute is about a גזירה. The question is whether cabbage should be forbidden so that people do not mix it up with other ספיחין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that cabbage ספיחין fall under the general topic of ספיחין. The question is only whether the איסור is applied to cabbage too. The חכמים include it to avoid confusion with other ספיחין. רבי שמעון holds that cabbage is so different that no one will confuse it, so no גזירה is needed.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone follows רבי עקיבא that ספיחין are forbidden. The חכמים extend the איסור to cabbage with a גזירה. רבי שמעון does not, because cabbage is unlike other vegetables. That is why רבי שמעון בן יוחי ate cabbage ספיחין in the story.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not deny the איסור of ספיחין. He only refuses to apply the גזירה to cabbage.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:
We decree on cabbage after-growths
because of other after-growths in general,
and Rabbi Shimon holds:
We do not decree on cabbage after-growths
because of after-growths in general.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: גָּזְרִינַן סְפִיחֵי כְרוּב אַטּוּ שְׁאָר סְפִיחֵי דְעָלְמָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is whether to make a גזירה on cabbage ספיחין because of other ספיחין: the חכמים do, and רבי שמעון does not.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the easy case first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and grants that the first case makes sense. Someone who comes to a non-working place keeps their stricter custom and does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who travels from a place, etc.' It makes sense for someone who goes from a place that works to a place that does not work. We give him the strict rules of the place he went to, and 'a person should not deviate, because of dispute.' So he should not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה and explains the case that is easy to understand. This is a setup: it prepares the challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a town that does not work on ערב פסח, a visitor who works would stand out and could cause friction. So the phrase אל ישנה אדם מפני המחלוקת fits this case well: he follows the locals and does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (sets up an easy case before a hard one)
The strict practices of a place
A person should not act differently from the locals, because it causes conflict

phrases.english: 'One who travels from a place, etc.'
phrases.notes: Quoting the opening words of the משנה

phrases.english: It makes sense for one who goes from a place where they work
to a place where they do not work

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתְנִין עָלָיו חוּמְרֵי מָקוֹם שֶׁהָלַךְ לְשָׁם,
phrases.english: we impose on him the stringencies of the place he went to,
and 'a person should not deviate because of dispute'
so he should not work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the ספיחין side discussion to the משנה about local customs of working on ערב פסח
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase אל ישנה אדם מפני המחלוקת in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: this establishes the case where the phrase clearly fits, before showing the case where it seems not to fit

steps.title: The hard case: should the visitor work?
steps.stepSummary: If the phrase also covers the reverse case, a visitor from a non-working place should work in a working town. But the משנה says he keeps the stricter custom of both places.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about someone who goes from a place that does not work to a place that does work? Should we say 'a person should not deviate because of dispute,' so he should work? But you said: 'We give him the strict rules of the place he went to and the strict rules of the place he left'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks its real question. It points out that the 'don't deviate' phrase seems to clash with the rule of keeping both places' stringencies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'don't deviate' covers the second case, it would tell the visitor to work like the locals. Yet the same משנה says he keeps the strictness of his home town, which means he does not work. The two statements seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: But you said! (points to a contradiction)

phrases.english: But from a place where they do not work
to a place where they do work,

phrases.aramaic: אַל יְשַׁנֶּה אָדָם מִפְּנֵי הַמַּחְלוֹקֶת וְנַעְבֵּיד?
phrases.english: does 'a person should not deviate because of dispute' mean he should work?

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמְרַתְּ: ״נוֹתְנִין עָלָיו חוּמְרֵי מָקוֹם שֶׁהָלַךְ לְשָׁם
phrases.english: But you said: 'We impose on him the stringencies of the place he went to'
'and the stringencies of the place he left'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין לְמָקוֹם שֶׁעוֹשִׂין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא/אלא structure begun in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying אל ישנה אדם מפני המחלוקת to the second case of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here the phrase would require working, but the rule of keeping both places' stringencies requires not working, so the משנה seems to contradict itself

steps.title: אביי: the phrase refers only to the first case
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that 'don't deviate' goes only on the first case of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It refers to the first part.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by limiting the phrase to the first case, the visitor who comes to a non-working town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the phrase is attached only to the רישא, it never tells the visitor in a working town to work. That visitor just keeps his home town's stringency, so the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: It goes on the first clause
אביי, an אמורא who often disagrees with רבא

phrases.english: אביי said: It refers to the first clause.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a phrase in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase אל ישנה applies to both cases
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase applies only to the רישא, a visitor arriving in a non-working place

steps.title: רבא: the phrase can refer to the second case
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the phrase does go on the סיפא. It means that not working there is not considered a deviation that causes dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, it refers to the last part, and this is what it means: In this case there is no problem of a change that causes dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer. He keeps the phrase on the second case but reads it in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי read the phrase as a command ('don't deviate'). רבא reads it as a reassurance: a visitor who refrains from work in a working town is not considered to be deviating at all. So he may keep his strict home custom, and the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: It goes on the last clause
And this is what it means (introduces a new reading)
A change or deviation from local practice

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the visitor should work. He says the visitor may refrain from work, because refraining does not count as a deviation that stirs up conflict.

phrases.english: רבא said: Really, it refers to the last clause,
and this is what it means:
In this case there is no issue of a deviation that causes dispute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the קשיא of step 10, different from אביי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase is a command to follow the locals, which would mean working
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase means that refraining from work is not a dispute-causing deviation

steps.title: Why not working does not look like a deviation
steps.stepSummary: רבא heads off a concern: onlookers won't think he holds work is forbidden. They will just think he is one of the many idle people in the market.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are you saying, that someone who sees him will say work is forbidden? No, they will say: How many idle people there are in the market!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא supports his answer by raising a possible worry and rejecting it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that people seeing him not work would think he considers work forbidden, which would be a public disagreement with local custom. רבא says no: people who don't work are common in any market, so no one reads it as a halachic statement.

keyTerms.meaning: What are you saying? (introduces a concern in order to reject it)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: אל ישנה applies only to the first case. רבא: it applies to the second case too, because refraining from work is not a visible deviation, since people assume he is just idle.

phrases.english: What are you saying —
that one who sees him will say work is forbidden?
Rather, they will say:
How many idle people there are in the market!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא אָמְרַתְּ הָרוֹאֶה אוֹמֵר מְלָאכָה אֲסוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and defends רבא's reading in step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting a hidden concern about how onlookers will interpret his behavior
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Refraining would look like a public claim that work is forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: Onlookers assume he is simply idle, so there is no dispute

steps.title: רב ספרא asks about places that know the calendar
steps.stepSummary: A new topic begins. רב ספרא tells רבי אבא that communities like his already know the fixed calendar, which sets up a question about יום טוב שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said to רבי אבא: For people like us, who know when the month is fixed,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new discussion about יום טוב שני של גלויות. This line only sets up the question, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יום טוב שני began because distant communities did not know which day ראש חודש was fixed. רב ספרא points out that his community now knows the calendar, so the doubt no longer exists. That raises the question of how they should treat the second day.

keyTerms.meaning: The fixing of the new month (ראש חודש)
The second day of יום טוב kept outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סָפְרָא לְרַבִּי אַבָּא:
phrases.english: רב ספרא said to רבי אבא:
For people like us, who know the fixing of the month,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סָפְרָא לְרַבִּי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from customs of working on ערב פסח to the related topic of יום טוב שני
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How communities that already know the calendar should treat יום טוב שני (the question continues on the next amud)
